statements.attributed: replacing a significant part of iron cations with cations of other elements is very promising because it can lead to a change in the main magnetic parameters because of the reconfiguration of structural features
statements.quote: The idea of replacing a significant part of iron cations with cations of other elements is very promising since it can lead to a change in the main magnetic parameters because of the reconfiguration of structural features.

statements.attributed: multi-element substitution leads to a high configurational entropy of mixing of iron sublattice cations which forms a resulting chemical phase with increased stability
statements.quote: In the case of multi-element substitution, a high configurational entropy of mixing of iron sublattice cations will form, and the resulting chemical phase will have increased stability. A high configurational mixing entropy will increase the entropy of the formed phase and decrease its Gibbs energy. The existence and stability of this phase will be the most probable.

statements.attributed: the solubility of cations of the same type on simple substitution is not high and reaches several units even for cations with an ionic radius smaller than the iron cation radius
statements.cited_system: substituted M-type hexaferrites BaFe12–x Al x O19 (x ⩽ 1.2)
statements.quote: The solubility of cations of the same type on simple substitution is not high and reaches several units even for cations with an ionic radius smaller than the iron cation radius. The use of several cations with a radius both greater and less than the radius of the iron cation with complex multication substitution significantly increases their solubility limit and leads to the formation of solid solutions with increased stability and unusual physicochemical properties.

statements.quote: The LAS method was used to find the saturation magnetization value. It determines the magnetization in a field close to the saturation one.

statements.attributed: reports a saturation magnetization of ~100 emu/g for unsubstituted strontium hexaferrite
statements.quote: One of the features is the negligible saturation magnetization for all the obtained samples in comparison with unsubstituted strontium hexaferrite, for which it can reach ∼100 emu/g. In our case, with deep substitution, magnetic dilution of the iron sublattice is observed, which leads to a low saturation magnetization.

statements.attributed: provides the formula k = 1.94*Ms*√tan(φ) for the anisotropy coefficient
statements.quote: The k coefficient of magnetic crystallographic anisotropy was found as k = 1.94∗Ms∗√tan(φ), as a proportional product of the saturation magnetization Ms and the square root of the tangent of the angle φ, which represents the angle of inclination of the linear extrapolation of the M(H−2) magnetization to the abscissa axis.

statements.attributed: provides the formula Ha = 2*k/Ms for the anisotropy field
statements.quote: The Ha anisotropy field was found as the ratio of twice the coefficient of magnetic crystallographic anisotropy to the saturation magnetization Ha = 2∗k/Ms.

statements.attributed: reports a Néel temperature of ~730 K for unsubstituted SrFe12O19
statements.quote: The highest Tmo magnetic ordering temperature of ∼381.8 K recorded for the A3 sample is much lower than the Néel temperature of ∼730 K for unsubstituted SrFe12O19.

statements.attributed: provides a method to estimate the generalized size of clusters using Tf and k
statements.quote: The generalized size of existing clusters can be estimated using the Tf freezing temperature and the k magnetic crystallographic anisotropy coefficient. In our case, it reaches ∼400 nm.
